rule: Automated reviewer identity is single-sourced in the reviewer-identity.jq module and every consumer routes through it
description:
Automated Reviewer identity lives in exactly one place: plugin/skills/github-review-loop/scripts/reviewer-identity.jq. The module derives the Automated Reviewer set from evidence the pull request shows (Bot review authors and Bot THUMBS_UP reactors) plus the logins configured in HIVEMIND_PR_REVIEWERS, and owns every identity predicate over it (`strip_bot`, `is_bot`, `is_self`, `configured_reviewers`, `automated_reviewer_set`, `is_automated_reviewer`, `reviewer_matches_filter`, `is_review_approval`, `is_retired_filter`). It names no reviewer product and no product login. Consumers reach it two ways: the jq filter fix-history-classify.jq, the jq programs inside pr-change-detect-poll.sh, the retired-filter gates in prefilter.sh, fetch-normalize.sh and react-marker.sh, and the noise author predicate inside react-marker.sh carry `include "reviewer-identity";`, and every shell call site that runs one of them passes the module search path with `jq -L <dir holding the module>` (prefilter.sh, fetch-normalize.sh, pr-change-detect-poll.sh and react-marker.sh directly; fetch-normalize.sh's classifier run through _shared/fetch-normalize-core.sh, which derives that dir from the classifier path). The identity predicates gate on the account type, so every GraphQL selection whose rows reach a type-gated predicate requests `author { login __typename }`, or `__typename` on reactor nodes. This fixture owns three axes. (1) CANONICAL CLAIM. The source pin sits on the set derivation `def automated_reviewer_set(` in reviewer-identity.jq: deleting or renaming it turns the suite red. The derivation body is pinned on the span `select(is_bot(.login; .type)) | strip_bot(.login) | ascii_downcase | select(. != "" and . != "github-actions") ] + $configured | unique;`, which carries three load-bearing clauses: only Bot-account evidence rows enter the set, so dropping the `is_bot` select admits every human reviewer; `github-actions`, the generic CI identity any workflow step posts as, is dropped from the evidence, so dropping or inverting that compare admits arbitrary CI output and widens the prompt-injection surface to anything a workflow can write; and the configured logins are added to the evidence set, so dropping `+ $configured` silently ignores HIVEMIND_PR_REVIEWERS. Set membership is pinned on `def is_automated_reviewer($login; $type; $set): is_bot($login; $type) and`: a set member counts only on a Bot account, so a configured login held by a human User never matches, and dropping that gate turns the suite red. The self predicate is pinned on `def is_self($login; $type; $self): $type == "User"`, a span that carries both the definition name and its account-type gate, so deleting or renaming `is_self` or dropping the `User` type gate (reverting self identity to a login-only compare) turns the suite red. The Bot-account predicate is pinned on its whole definition `def is_bot($login; $type): $type == "Bot" or (($login // "") | endswith("[bot]"))`: the REST reactions endpoint reports a bot reactor's `user.type` as `User` while its login keeps the reserved `[bot]` suffix (a GitHub login is alphanumerics and hyphens, so no human login can carry it), so a Bot account is typed `Bot` OR suffixed, and deleting or renaming `is_bot`, or dropping either arm (reverting to a type-only gate that rejects a REST-typed bot thumbs-up, or to a suffix-only gate), turns the suite red. These pins prove each definition's word sequence is present, never that a predicate or consumer calls it: the gates that use `is_bot` are proved by behaviour, by the Bot-account and set truth tables in tools/test_fix_history_classify.sh and by `approval:rest-user-typed-bot-thumbs-up-approves`, `approval:every-bot-shape-approves-identically` and `approval:ci-identity-only-when-listed` in tools/test_change_detect_poll.sh. (2) CONSUMER WIRING. pr-change-detect-poll.sh is pinned once per identity program. Its set derivation is pinned on `reviewer_set=$(printf '%s
%s
%s
' "$snapshot_review_rows" "$review_rows" "$reaction_rows" \ | jq -s -c -L "$SCRIPT_DIR" --arg reviewers "${HIVEMIND_PR_REVIEWERS-}" ' include "reviewer-identity"; automated_reviewer_set(.; $reviewers)`, which carries all three evidence streams, the configured value, the search path, the include and the module call, so dropping an evidence stream or the configured value, or replacing the derivation with an inline list, stops the match. Its three filter and approval programs are pinned on spans covering the `-L "$SCRIPT_DIR"` invocation, the `--argjson set "$reviewer_set"` that hands each program the one derived set, and the `include "reviewer-identity";` that opens the program body, so dropping the search path, the set, or the include at any call site stops the match. The two approval programs share the same invocation text, so their pins also carry the assignment and input each one reads (`review_approved=$(printf '%s' "$review_rows" \` and `thumbs_approved=$(printf '%s' "$reaction_rows" \`): each pin can match only its own call site, and one surviving call site cannot keep the other's pin green. prefilter.sh is pinned on its classifier invocation `jq -r -L "$SCRIPT_DIR" -f "$CLASSIFY_FILTER" --arg login "$SELF_LOGIN" --arg filter "$REVIEWER_FILTER" \ --arg reviewers "${HIVEMIND_PR_REVIEWERS-}"`. _shared/fetch-normalize-core.sh is pinned on its classifier invocation `jq -c -L "$classify_module_dir" -f "$classify_filter_path" --arg login "$self_login" --arg filter "$reviewer_filter" --arg reviewers "$configured_reviewers"` and on the derivation that binds that dir to the classifier's own directory, so pointing `-L` anywhere else, or dropping the configured value, fails. react-marker.sh is pinned twice for its noise author check: on the invocation `jq -e -L "$SCRIPT_DIR" \ --arg filter "$NOISE_FILTER" \ --arg raw "${HIVEMIND_PR_REVIEWERS-}" \ "$NOISE_AUTHOR_PREDICATE"`, which carries the search path, the configured value and the program it runs, and on `NOISE_AUTHOR_PREDICATE=' include "reviewer-identity";`, the include that opens that program's body. The retired-filter gate is pinned in pr-change-detect-poll.sh, prefilter.sh, fetch-normalize.sh and react-marker.sh, each on a span from its `jq -n` invocation with `-L "$SCRIPT_DIR"` through `include "reviewer-identity"; is_retired_filter($filter)`, so a consumer that drops the module call, for example to compare against the retired value inline, stops the match; the closure test in tools/test_fix_history_classify.sh covers reintroduction of the retired literal itself. The query literals are pinned per selection on spans that include the neighbouring field list (`nodes { author { login __typename } body url reactionGroups` and so on), because the bare substring `author { login __typename }` also appears in header comments and would survive the query losing `__typename`. In prefilter.sh and fetch-normalize.sh each comment and review selection is pinned whole, through `lastEditedAt reactions(content: EYES, last: 20) { nodes { content createdAt user { login __typename } } }`: the classifier counts a handled mark only from a reaction whose user is self per the type-keyed `is_self`, and only while the node's `lastEditedAt` is null or earlier than that mark, so dropping `lastEditedAt`, the reaction connection, or the reactor's `__typename` stops the match. The evidence selections the classifier builds the set from are pinned in both files on `latestReviews(first: 100) { nodes { author { login __typename } } } reactionGroups { content reactors(first: 100) { nodes { __typename ... on Bot { login } ... on User { login } } } }`: `is_bot` gates each evidence row on its type, so dropping either connection or either `__typename` silently empties the evidence set. react-marker.sh's binding query selects the PR evidence and the node author with identical text under both inline fragments, and its noise author check reads them through `automated_reviewer_set`, `is_bot` and `reviewer_matches_filter`, so each selection is pinned on a span that starts at its own fragment (`... on IssueComment { pullRequest { state headRefName headRepository { id } latestReviews(first: 100) ...` through `author { login __typename } reactionGroups`, and the same under `... on PullRequestReview {`): one surviving fragment cannot keep the other's pin green. The poll's comment and review-thread selections feed the type-keyed self predicate `is_self`, so they are pinned too, on spans that include the parent connection (`comments(last: 50) { totalCount nodes { databaseId author { login __typename } } }` and `comments(last: 1) { nodes { databaseId author { login __typename } } }`), because the bare node selection `nodes { databaseId author { login __typename } }` occurs in both and a bare pin would survive either one losing `__typename`. The poll judges a review approval from GitHub's per-author latest reviews through an exhaustive paginated walk in a query of its own (gh follows one paginated connection per query), so its selection is pinned on the span `latestReviews(first: 100, after: $endCursor) { pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } nodes { state author { login __typename } comments { totalCount } } }`, which carries the connection name, its page size, the cursor argument, the page-info selection gh follows to the next page, the review state, the account type, and the inline review comment count `is_review_approval` reads to judge a COMMENTED review: dropping any of them stops the match. `first: 100` is the page size, not a bound on how many authors are read. The pagination contract is also enforced behaviourally: the fake gh in tools/test_change_detect_poll.sh serves pages after the first only when the whitespace-normalized query declares `$endCursor: String`, passes `after: $endCursor`, and selects `pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }`, and it serves a failed later page as a non-zero exit, so `approval:latest-reviews-every-page-read` goes red when the walk stops at page 1 and `approval:latest-reviews-partial-walk-fails-closed` goes red when a partial walk is judged instead of failing the capture. The poll reads its THUMBS_UP evidence over REST, not GraphQL, so that read has no query pin; `approval:rest-user-typed-bot-thumbs-up-approves` covers it. RESIDUALS for the latestReviews pin: it proves the selection is present in the query text, never that the approval derivation uses it; it does not carry the `$endCursor: String` declaration or the `--paginate` flag, which only the behaviour cases cover; and those cases run against a fake gh that models gh's documented pagination contract, so a divergence between that model and real gh is invisible to this suite. These query pins are the ONLY guard on query drift: the behaviour tests inject payloads and bypass the live GraphQL queries entirely, so a query that stopped requesting `__typename` would make every type-gated predicate silently reject every author while the tests stay green. (3) INCLUDE IS LIVE CODE, AND NO SECOND COPY. set_check extracts, from lines whose first non-blank token is the literal (comment lines begin with `#` and never match), either `include "reviewer-identity";` or a definition of one of the module's nine names (`def strip_bot`, `def is_bot`, `def is_self`, `def configured_reviewers`, `def automated_reviewer_set`, `def is_automated_reviewer`, `def reviewer_matches_filter`, `def is_review_approval`, `def is_retired_filter`). fix-history-classify.jq and pr-change-detect-poll.sh are checked in `equal` mode against the single-member set {include}: this proves the include sits on a real code line (fix-history-classify.jq also names the include inside a header comment, so a plain presence pin there would survive deleting the live include), and any redefinition of a module name in those files is an extra and fails. prefilter.sh, fetch-normalize.sh, _shared/fetch-normalize-core.sh, and react-marker.sh are checked in `subset` mode against the same set, so a module name redefined inside any of their embedded jq programs fails; `subset` accepts an empty set, so in those files the include's presence rests on the consumer pins, not on the set_check. The capture group is a fixed literal alternation rather than a negated-delimiter class because the axis is presence of one known literal plus absence of known definition literals, not membership of an enumerable marker set: a broad `def [a-z_]+` capture would also see each consumer's own legitimate helper definitions. RESIDUALS, stated plainly: these pins claim word-sequence presence in the named files, never meaning, and never that the code executes. A NEW consumer file not named here is invisible: a new script that queries review authors without `__typename`, invokes the classifier without `-L`, or derives its own reviewer set is not caught (set_check `files` is a literal list with no glob expansion). A rewrite that keeps every pinned substring while bypassing the module, for example matching inline login literals in a consumer that still includes the module, is not caught by this fixture; the closure test in tools/test_fix_history_classify.sh covers reintroduction of known reviewer product logins, the `github-actions` literal, the `[bot]` strip literal and the retired-filter literal in the module and the consumer files it names. A second copy of a module def under a different name, or one whose `def` is wrapped so the name does not follow `def ` on the same line, is invisible to the set_check because extraction is line-scoped and case-sensitive. A consumer that drops its `is_self` call in favour of a login-only compare keeps this fixture green; the self-compare closure check in tools/test_fix_history_classify.sh covers login-only self compares in the consumer files it names, and a NEW consumer file is invisible to it as well. The react-marker.sh pins prove the noise author program is loaded with the module and given the configured value, not that it calls `automated_reviewer_set`, `is_bot` and `reviewer_matches_filter`; the noise cases in tools/test_react_marker.sh (`noise:refused-human-all`, `noise:refused-status-bot-without-evidence`, `noise:accepted-configured-bot-automated`) cover a check that stops gating on any of them. The evidence-selection pins prove the evidence is requested, not that the classifier reads it; `case28:evidence-default` and `case28:evidence-configured` in tools/test_fix_history_classify.sh cover that. The reaction-selection pins prove `lastEditedAt` and the reactor's `__typename` are requested, not that the classifier compares them; `case26:marked-then-edited` in tools/test_fix_history_classify.sh covers the edit-time comparison.

thumbs_approved=$(printf '%s' "$reaction_rows" \ | jq -s -r -L "$SCRIPT_DIR" --arg login "$SELF_LOGIN" --arg filter "$REVIEWER_FILTER" \ --argjson set "$reviewer_set" ' include "reviewer-identity";

latestReviews(first: 100) { nodes { author { login __typename } } } reactionGroups { content reactors(first: 100) { nodes { __typename ... on Bot { login } ... on User { login } } } }
